title: Nomilin Rewires mTOR-Driven Immunometabolism via DDIT4 to Restrain Psoriasis.
authors: Kim, Ha Eun; Lee, Seung Taek; Park, Hee-Suk; Lee, Hyun-Su; Lee, Jong Yeong; Kim, Dae-Ki; Roh, Si-Gyun; Nam, Kyung-Hwa; Kim, Sang-Hyun; Choi, Jin Kyeong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究柠檬苦素类化合物Nomilin通过DDIT4-mTOR轴调节免疫代谢治疗银屑病，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Nomilin, a citrus-derived limonoid belonging to the tetranortriterpenoid family, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects; however, its therapeutic relevance and underlying mechanisms in psoriasis remain unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of nomilin in 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13-acetate (TPA)- and imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse models, IL-17A-stimulated primary human keratinocytes, Th17-polarized CD4(+) T cells, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with psoriasis. Nomilin markedly alleviated epidermal hyperplasia and inflammatory symptoms, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and psoriasis-associated mediators, and reduced the expansion of inflammatory myeloid and Th1/Th17 cells in lesional skin. Mechanistically, nomilin decreased glucose uptake, glycolytic activity, oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial mass, and mitochondrial ROS production, thereby preventing metabolic overactivation and mitochondrial dysfunction. At the molecular level, nomilin upregulated DDIT4 and inhibited mTOR signaling, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation of mTOR, RAPTOR, p70S6K, and 4EBP1. Genetic silencing of DDIT4 abrogated the anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects of nomilin in keratinocytes, while skin-specific DDIT4 knockdown markedly attenuated its therapeutic efficacy in vivo, demonstrating an essential role for DDIT4 in nomilin-mediated mTOR suppression. Furthermore, molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) analyses revealed a direct interaction between nomilin and DDIT4. In addition, nomilin suppressed Th17 differentiation and reduced TNF-alpha-, IFN-gamma-, and IL-17A-producing CD4(+) T cells in PBMCs from patients with psoriasis. Collectively, these findings identify nomilin as a modulator of the DDIT4-mTOR axis that alleviates psoriasis-like inflammation through the rewiring of pathogenic immunometabolic programs and highlight its potential as a therapeutic strategy for psoriasis.
abstract_zh: 诺米林（nomilin）是一种源自柑橘的柠檬苦素类化合物，属于四降三萜类家族，已被报道具有抗炎和抗氧化作用；然而，其在银屑病中的治疗相关性及潜在机制仍不清楚。在此，我们研究了诺米林在12-O-十四烷酰佛波醇-13-乙酸酯（TPA）和咪喹莫特（IMQ）诱导的银屑病样小鼠模型、IL-17A刺激的原代人角质形成细胞、Th17极化的CD4(+) T细胞以及银屑病患者的周围血单核细胞（PBMCs）中的作用。诺米林显著减轻了表皮增生和炎症症状，抑制了促炎细胞因子和银屑病相关介质，并减少了病变皮肤中炎性髓系细胞和Th1/Th17细胞的扩增。机制上，诺米林降低了葡萄糖摄取、糖酵解活性、氧化磷酸化、线粒体质量和线粒体ROS产生，从而阻止了代谢过度激活和线粒体功能障碍。在分子水平上，诺米林上调了DDIT4并抑制了mTOR信号通路，表现为mTOR、RAPTOR、p70S6K和4EBP1磷酸化水平的降低。DDIT4的基因沉默消除了诺米林在角质形成细胞中的抗炎和代谢效应，而皮肤特异性DDIT4敲低显著减弱了其在体内的治疗效果，证明了DDIT4在诺米林介导的mTOR抑制中的关键作用。此外，分子对接和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）揭示了诺米林与DDIT4之间的直接相互作用。另外，诺米林抑制了Th17分化，并减少了银屑病患者PBMCs中产生TNF-α、IFN-γ和IL-17A的CD4(+) T细胞。综合来看，这些发现将诺米林鉴定为DDIT4-mTOR轴的调节剂，通过重塑致病性免疫代谢程序来缓解银屑病样炎症，并突显了其作为银屑病治疗策略的潜力。
